answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a staked-identity bond: each agent locks collateral to earn a single vote. Splitting into many fakes gains nothing, because every new identity must post its own bond, so an attacker's cost rises linearly with each Sybil added. Detection triggers a slash that burns the bond and follows the collateral, not the name, so renaming a rogue agent basalt, yarrow, or plume cannot escape it. To buy a thousand votes an attacker must lock a thousand separate bonds, making a takeover far dearer than honest work.
